before.text:
Time Machine

Replay a hypothetical move for Robert with an information cutoff

Choose a past date. The rule checks and figures use only data rows available on that date. What happened afterwards stays hidden until you ask to reveal it.

What this replay can and cannot show

The language model’s knowledge is not erased. Figures come from date-filtered data, but wording may reflect what happened later.
Prices are adjusted and macro series are revised: this is not the data as originally published on that date.
The asset universe was selected later, among names that are large today.
This is a historical simulation, not a validation of any forecast and not an offline replay of a real decision.
Information cutoff

Supported cutoff dates: Nov 22, 2022 → Aug 18, 2026. Earlier dates lack the history the calculations need; later dates leave too little data to reveal.

2025-02-19: before the largest later fall
2025-02-19
Selected with hindsight for demonstration: the eligible day followed by the largest fall of SPY within the next 60 trading days in this dataset. The selection never enters the decision.
2022-12-30: end of 2022

Cutoff date

Notices from the API

The language model may know what happened after the selected date. Numbers come from date-filtered data, but wording could reflect later knowledge.
Computed on the available window only (from 2021-11-12 in the starter data). Other periods would give different values.
The asset universe was chosen in 2026 among names that are large today, which flatters historical results.
Prices come from Yahoo Finance and are not exchange-certified. Adjusted closes change when data is re-downloaded.
US macro values are the latest revised figures, not as first published.
